label: PF Backlog 600
title: Expose doc-driven backlog ingest via a Go capability service (generic surface); tooling becomes a client

brief.what_adds: A generic Go capability service exposing context:from-doc that applies via the backlog HTTP API
brief.problem: Doc-driven backlog ingest is tooling-only, so internal/external actors cannot consume it

objective: Expose doc-driven backlog ingest via a Go capability service (generic surface); tooling becomes a client
acceptance_criteria: Objective achieved: Expose doc-driven backlog ingest via a Go capability service (generic surface); tooling becomes a client
in_scope: Expose doc-driven backlog ingest via a Go capability service (generic surface); tooling becomes a client
approach: Expose doc-driven backlog ingest via a Go capability service (generic surface); tooling becomes a client
verification: Objective achieved: Expose doc-driven backlog ingest via a Go capability service (generic surface); tooling becomes a client

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the existing Go core/backlog and product_ingestion modules with a new HTTP route POST /api/v1/backlog/epics/{epic_id}/context:from-doc delegating to the shared ingest function; the doc-parsing tooling is refactored into a thin client of this capability service.
conflict_findings: Possible concurrent edits to core/backlog.py with BI-PF-1396
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1396 defines the same endpoint — scope this item as the service+tooling split while 1396 covers endpoint acceptance
core/product_ingestion.py already performs plan-.md projection — reuse, do not reimplement
analysis.rationale: The capability already exists in-process; the gap is exposing it via an HTTP surface and making doc tooling call it instead of inlining logic — a pure EXTEND of existing Go modules.
assumptions: Existing /api/v1/backlog routes provide the auth+error envelope to reuse
Tooling currently invokes ingest logic in-process
Dry-run defaults apply on the service side
risks: Endpoint contract drift between service and tooling client
Dry-run default semantics could be bypassed by client
Auth model for internal consumers not yet defined
evidence: Candidate list includes core/backlog.py and existing /api/v1/backlog endpoints
BI-PF-1396 backlog item explicitly specifies the endpoint
Existing groom/dry-run patterns already present in route set
missing_info: Which specific tooling binary/script is the client
Auth requirements for internal vs external callers
Whether dry-run should be a query param or body flag

api_impact.reason: retrofit assessment (ADR-0007): no external API consumer recorded; treated as internal until an API surface is required (then set needs_api=true with routes)
